name: GTDB_search_taxon
description: Search GTDB taxa by partial name, returning rank-prefixed names (d__, p__, c__, o__, f__, g__, s__). The upstream endpoint accepts at most 100 matches and has no offset. When data.possible_more is true, the result may be incomplete and the query must be narrowed; data.complete_known is true only when fewer than limit matches are returned.

query.description: Partial taxon name to search for (e.g., 'Lachnospiraceae', 'Escherichia', 'Bacillota'). Case-insensitive.

limit.description: Maximum number of results per rank (default: 20, max: 100)

matches.description: Matching GTDB taxon names with rank prefixes

complete_known.description: True when the completeness of the result is known rather than assumed.

limit.description: Page size applied to this call.

limit_scope.description: What the limit applies to, e.g. 'per_rank'. A limit applied per group returns more rows than the number suggests.

pagination_supported.description: False when the upstream offers no way to page, so a capped result cannot be continued at all - the cap is the end of what this tool can return.

possible_more.description: True when more records may exist but the upstream does not say.

rank_counts.description: How many matches at each rank, keyed by the rank's letter. With limit_scope 'per_rank' this is what says how the limit was spent.

name: GTDB_get_species
description: Get a recoverable page of genomes in a GTDB species cluster. total_genomes is exact because GTDB returns the complete cluster; continue with next_offset while has_more is true.

species.description: Species name WITHOUT the s__ prefix (e.g., 'Escherichia coli', 'Hydrogenothermus marinus', 'Bacillus subtilis')

max_genomes.description: Maximum number of genomes to return (default: 20). Species clusters can have thousands of genomes.

offset.description: Zero-based genome offset. Continue with next_offset.

total_genomes.description: Total number of genomes in this species cluster

genomes_shown.description: Number of genomes in the response (may be limited)

genomes.description: Genome entries in the species cluster

gtdb_species_rep.description: Whether this is the GTDB species representative genome

name: GTDB_get_taxon_info
description: Get information about a GTDB taxon including its rank, total genome count, higher-rank lineage, and release history. GTDB uses rank prefixes: d__ (domain), p__ (phylum), c__ (class), o__ (order), f__ (family), g__ (genus), s__ (species). For example, f__Lachnospiraceae returns its rank (Family), genome count, and lineage (Bacteria > Bacillota > Clostridia > Lachnospirales). Also returns the full lineage breakdown from domain to species. Useful for understanding where a taxon fits in the GTDB tree and how many genomes support it.

taxon.description: GTDB taxon name with rank prefix (e.g., 'f__Lachnospiraceae', 'd__Bacteria', 'g__Escherichia', 's__Escherichia coli'). Use GTDB_search_taxon to find valid names.

rank.description: Taxonomic rank (Domain, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species)

n_genomes.description: Total number of genomes classified under this taxon

higher_ranks.description: Parent taxa from domain down to parent rank

in_releases.description: GTDB releases this taxon appears in

lineage.description: Full lineage from domain (d) to species (s), keys: d, p, c, o, f, g, s

name: GTDB_search_genomes
description: Search for prokaryotic genomes in GTDB by organism name. A multi-word query (e.g. a binomial like 'Mycobacterium tuberculosis') is first matched precisely, requiring EVERY term of the query to appear in the genome's name or taxonomy; 'match_type' is then 'exact'. If nothing matches the whole query, the tool falls back to GTDB's loose search, which matches ANY term of the query and therefore returns a broader taxon (often just the genus) or a different species; that case is reported as 'match_type': 'broad' with a top-level 'note', and 'total_results' then counts the broader match rather than the queried organism -- always read 'match_type' and 'total_results_scope' before quoting a count or trusting a result. Results also match against the whole taxonomic clade rather than organism-name text alone, so exact/prefix name matches are ranked first within a page. Returns genome accessions with both NCBI and GTDB taxonomy classifications, allowing comparison between the two taxonomic systems. Each result shows the genome accession (GCA/GCF), NCBI organism name, NCBI taxonomy, GTDB taxonomy, and whether the genome is a GTDB species representative. Pagination is strictly one-based (page 0 is rejected because the live API treats it anomalously and can return the entire result set) with pages up to 1000 records; the response reports total_results, total_pages, has_more, and next_page. Useful for finding genome accessions, exploring taxonomic reclassifications, and linking genomes to the GTDB taxonomy.

query.description: Search query for organism name (e.g., 'Escherichia', 'Staphylococcus aureus', 'Lactobacillus')

page.description: One-based page number (default 1). Never use 0; continue with metadata.next_page.

items_per_page.description: Number of results per page (default 10, max 1000).

match_type.description: How the results relate to the query. 'exact': every returned genome matches every term of the query. 'broad': nothing matched the whole query, so these results match only part of it (typically the genus) and are NOT the queried organism -- see 'note'. 'none': GTDB holds no matching genome.

total_results.description: Total number of genomes in the match described by 'match_type'. When match_type is 'broad' this is the count for the broader match, NOT for the queried organism -- see 'total_results_scope'.

total_results_scope.description: Plain-language statement of exactly what 'total_results' counts

note.description: Present when match_type is 'broad' or 'none': explains that the results are not the queried organism and that total_results must not be reported as its genome count

isGtdbSpeciesRep.description: Whether this is a GTDB species representative

isNcbiTypeMaterial.description: Whether this is NCBI type material

count.description: Number of results on this page

has_more.description: True when more records match than this response carries. The field that says the answer is a page and not the whole set.

truncated.description: True when the result was cut by a cap rather than reaching the end of the data.

next_page.description: Page number to request next, or null at the end.

total_pages.description: How many pages the result spans, e.g. 10535. With items_per_page this is the only statement of the result's real size.

name: GTDB_get_genome
description: Get comprehensive metadata for a specific genome by NCBI accession from GTDB. Returns nucleotide statistics (genome size, GC%, contig count, N50), gene-level metrics (completeness via CheckM/CheckM2, contamination, SSU/LSU counts, protein count, coding density), NCBI metadata (assembly level, BioProject, BioSample, isolation source, geographic coordinates), and taxonomic history across GTDB releases. Useful for evaluating genome quality, finding genome properties, and tracking taxonomic changes across GTDB versions.

accession.description: NCBI genome accession (e.g., 'GCF_000005845.2' for E. coli K-12, 'GCF_000009045.1' for B. subtilis)

genome.description: The genome's own record: accession, name and taxonomy

metadata_nucleotide.description: Assembly statistics: contig count, N50, GC content and the rest

metadata_gene.description: Gene-level statistics including CheckM completeness and contamination - the two numbers that say whether a genome is usable

metadata_ncbi.description: NCBI assembly metadata for the genome, including its GenBank and RefSeq accessions

gtdb_taxonomy.description: GTDB taxonomic classification with domain to species rank assignments

taxon_history.description: Taxonomic history across GTDB releases, showing how classification changed over time
